etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Latin aberrāns, present active participle of aberrō (“go astray; err”), from ab (“from”) + errō (“to wander”). See aberr.
senses: Differing from the norm. [First attested sometime between the mid 16th century and the early 17th century.]
(sometimes figuratively) Straying from the right way; deviating from morality or truth. [First attested in the mid 18th century.]
A person or object that deviates from the rest of a group.
(biology) A group, individual, or structure that deviates from the usual or natural type, especially with an atypical chromosome number.
